articles.summary: We had early access from Google DeepMind to Gemini 3.5 Flash's native Computer Use tool and ran it on Cua-Bench's KiCad EDA suite. It posted the highest mean reward of any frontier model we tested - 0.267 - at Flash speed and cost, with pixel-accurate grounding and real analog-design reasoning.
articles.title: Evaluating Gemini 3.5 Flash on Computer-Use with Cua-Bench

articles.summary: Cua Driver now drives real Linux desktop apps in the background for any agent. It uses AT-SPI 2 over D-Bus for the accessibility tree, XTEST for input synthesis, and a painted agent cursor kept separate from your physical pointer, on X11 and XWayland.
articles.title: Inside Linux computer-use: AT-SPI, XTEST, and background agents
